title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6897 – Reuters estimate
body: The fixing mechanism matters most right now because its message has shifted over the past month. Through September, however, the midpoint has strengthened at a faster pace, narrowing its gap with market expectations and suggesting the central bank has eased its resistance to yuan gains. The fixing is still set weaker than models imply, so this looks like a loosening of the brakes rather than their removal. The balance Beijing is weighing is unchanged: a firmer currency supports capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness while the domestic economy remains soft. The gap between each day's fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the clearest guides to how far the PBOC is willing to let the yuan run.--- The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and after months of saying slow down, it has lately been saying go, gradually.Summary: The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets.

Despite hotter-than-expected inflation data, Treasury yields fell and yet tech stocks suffered all through the week. Is it a case of investors waking up to the struggles in market breadth and momentum? body: The direct market fallout is contained: QUBIC is a small-cap token, the loss is modest in dollar terms, and the selling has so far stayed confined to the token itself rather than spreading to the wider crypto market. The bigger near-term pressure is liquidity, with the network halted and exchanges suspending deposits and withdrawals, leaving holders unable to move tokens until the chain restarts. How the Computor vote handles restitution is likely to matter more for the token's recovery than the theft itself, since a clean, transparent outcome could steady confidence while a drawn-out freeze would add to doubts.
